full_judgment:
This Rule was issued upon an application under section 115(1) of the Code of  Civil Procedure calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 28-6-2007 passed by the Additional District Judge, Second Court, Narayanganj in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 36 of 2006 affirming the judgment and order dated 1-3-2006 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Fourth Court and House Rent Controller, Narayanganj, in House Rent Case No. 7 of 2005 rejecting the case should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. Petitioner, a tenant filed the case on 5-9-2005 for depositing the monthly rent in the name of the opposite parties with the House Rent Controller, Narayanganj under section 19(1)(a) of the House Rent Control Act, 1991, hereinafter referred to as Act, 1991. 

 3. The case of the petitioner in brief was that he was inducted in the case premises as monthly tenant on 1st October, 2003 at a monthly rent of Taka 5,500 including monthly rent of flat, electricity, Gas and water bill to be paid within 15 days of the next month upon an oral contract. It was further stated that the opposite parties took Taka 40,000 as advance from the petitioner granting receipt. It was further stated that the petitioner paid rent for the month of May, 2005 on 16-6-2005 and when rent for the month of July, 2005 was tendered the opposite parties refused to accept on 7-8-2005 and then again he requested the opposite parties to accept the rent for the month of July, 2005 on 27-8-2005, this time also they refused to accept. Then the petitioner sent the rent for the month of July, 2005 to the opposite parties through postal money order and on 31-8-2005 the same was returned back with the postal endorsement "Refused". Then he filed the instant case seeking permission to deposit the monthly rent. 

 4. The opposite parties contested the case by filing a written objection denying the allegations made in the petition contending that after preparing a written agreement for the tenancy was sent to the petitioner for his signature which he did not sign rather kept the same with him. It was their further case that they took Taka 40,000 as security money anti there was no condition for adjustment with the monthly rent. It was further stated that the petitioner used to pay monthly rent within the 15 days of the next month but for the month of May, 2005 he paid the rent on 16-6-2005 thereby he made himself a defaulter and since he was a defaulter and in unauthorised occupation of the case premises, he is not entitled under law to deposit the monthly rent with the House Rent Controller and the said case was liable to be rejected. 

 5. Both the parties examined 2 witnesses on each side and the petitioner adduced rent receipts and the Money Order receipts, which were marked as exhibits. 

 6. The House Rent Controller, Narayanganj hearing the parties and perusing the evidence on record by his judgment and order dated 1-3-2006 rejected the case holding that since the petitioner, a defaulter, was not entitled to deposit the monthly rent. However, he observed that the petitioner was entitled to get back the advance money Taka 40,000 from the opposite parties. The petitioner being aggrieved by the said judgment and order preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 36 of 2006 to the Court of District Judge, Narayanganj which on transfer was heard and disposed of by the Additional District Judge, Second Court, Narayanganj by the judgment and order dated 28-6-2007 dismissing the appeal and affirming those passed by the House Rent Controller, Narayanganj. However, by his order dated 3-7-2007 allowed the petitioner to deposit the monthly rent of June, 2007 in the House Rent Case No. 7 of 2005 in order to file civil revision before this Court. 

 7. Mr Shasti Sarker, the learned advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that both the House Rent Controller and the Court of appeal below misdirected themselves in rejecting the case in not granting permission to deposit the monthly rent of the case premises in the name of the opposite parties holding that since the petitioner being a defaulter he was not entitled to deposit the rent. He next submits that the House Rent Controller was not require to decide whether the petitioner was a defaulter which would to be decided in a suit for ejectment, if filed. He further submits that the House Rent Controller being a mere conduit pipe, he was required by law to allow the petitioner to deposit the monthly rent, if deposited in accordance with the provisions of section 19(1) (a) of the Act, 1991. He in support of his submissions referred to the decisions in the cases of Md Osman vs Fatema Khatoon reported in 41 DLR 270, Sheik Mohd Salimullah vs Shafiqul Alam reported in 43 DLR 113 and Rabeya Khatun vs Md Saidur Rahman reported in 56 DLR (AD) 19. He finally submits that the decisions of both the House Rent Controller and the Court of appeal below resulted in an error of law occasioning failure of justice, which are liable to be set aside. 

 8. Mr Abdul Quaim, the learned advocate appearing with Mr Sarder Abul Hossain, Advocate for the opposite parties, on the other hand, submits that though the petitioner is no doubt a defaulter yet he frankly concedes that both the House Rent Controller and the Court of appeal below were not correct in deciding the issue whether the petitioner was a defaulter or not, a subject matter to be decided in a regular suit for ejectment if instituted by the opposite parties. He also submits that the House Rent Controller is under legal obligation to permit the petitioner to deposit the monthly rent if he deposits in terms of section 19(1)(a) of the Act, 1991. He finally submits that the opposite parties have no objection if the petitioner is allowed to deposit the monthly rent of the case premises in favour of the opposite parties with the House Rent Controller, Narayanganj without any prejudice to the land lord. 

 10. Before entering into the case I like to quote section 19(1)(a) of the House Rent Control Act, 1991 which runs as follows: 

 11. Reading section 19(1)(ka) quoted above it appears that House Rent Controller is required only to examine whether the tenant is depositing the rent within 15 days from the date when the rent sent by money order returns back to the tenant on the refusal of the land lord to accept. Here, in the case in hand it appears that the petitioner tenant sent the monthly rent of July, 2005 by money order to the opposite parties—land lords on 27-8-2005 which was returned back to the petitioner with the postal endorsement "Refused" on 31-8-2005. Within 15 days from this date the petitioner was required to file the case with the House Rent Controller. There is no dispute that the petitioner has filed the case within time seeking permission to deposit the monthly rent with the House Rent Controller. It appears that both the House Rent Controller and the Court, of appeal below decided the case holding that the petitioner was a defaulter as he failed to pay rent to land lords—opposite parties within time. Neither the House Rent Controller nor the Court of appeal below were authorised by law to decide as to whether the petitioner was a defaulter which is the subject to be decided in a regular suit for eviction, if instituted by the opposite parties. The House Rent Controller being a conduit pipe, he was required to allow the petitioner to deposit the rent if he deposits the monthly rent in compliance with the provisions of section 19(1)(ka) of the Act, 1991. 

 12. For the discussions made above I am of the view that the learned House Rent Controller, Narayanganj and the Court of appeal below passed the impugned judgments and orders dismissing the House Rent Case resulted in an error of law occasioning failure of justice. 

 13. Since the opposite parties have no objection if the petitioner is allowed to deposit the monthly rent for the case premise in the name of the opposite parties without any prejudice to them the petitioner should be allowed to deposit the monthly rent with the House Rent Controller, Narayanganj in House Rent Case No. 7 of 2005 without any prejudice to the opposite parties. The House Rent Controller, Narayanganj is also directed to accept the monthly rent if deposited by the petitioner in accordance with the provisions of section 19(1)(ka) of the House Rent Control Act, 1991. 

 Communicate a copy of this judgment to the House Rent Controller, Narayanganj at once.
